There are no top-level commands, function calls, or code that would result in network activity, file system modifications, or data exfiltration when the file is sourced. The `source` and `sha256sums` arrays reference external URLs, but these are not downloaded or verified during `--printsrcinfo`. The use of `::` in the source array is standard for renaming downloaded files and does not imply execution. No obfuscated code, eval statements, or suspicious constructs appear in the global scope.
</details>
<evidence>

There are no eval, base64, curl-pipe-to-shell, git pull/reset, post-install hooks, or file operations outside the package destination. No red flags indicating injected malicious code or a supply-chain attack were found. The prebuilt binary itself is not audited here, which is inherent to -bin packages, but the packaging logic is clean.
</details>
